Biography

I am a PhD researcher in Artificial Intelligence at the University of Isfahan, Iran. I hold a bachelor’s degree in Software Engineering and a master’s degree in Artificial Intelligence and Robotics.

My research focuses on adaptive and interpretable machine learning, with particular attention to social interactions, uncertainty, and knowledge transfer. My earlier work established a foundation in recommender systems through trust modeling, collaborative filtering, member influence, and group decision-making.

That work has expanded toward adaptive group formation using multi-agent reinforcement learning and probabilistic representations of influence and preference changes. More recently, I have been exploring knowledge distillation, optimal transport, and the internal mechanisms of deep neural networks.

My current interests include geometric knowledge transfer, mechanistic interpretability, and causally informed, parameter-efficient adaptation of large language models for machine translation. Across these directions, I aim to connect mathematical modeling with practical learning algorithms.
